proposal.executive_summary: Sekisui Diagnostics develops, manufactures, and supplies diagnostic products and services including reagents and point-of-care tests. San Diego City College can partner with Sekisui Diagnostics to fulfill the employer's hiring needs for this role by leveraging the college's institutional assets. The college offers 86 courses with TOP codes that map to SOC 11-9121, the target occupation for this partnership. 10,248 students have taken courses in the departments offering these courses, indicating a talent pool that can be sourced to fulfill labor market demand.
proposal.occupational_demand: Sekisui Diagnostics's core hiring centers on Natural Sciences Managers (SOC 11-9121), an occupation with a median annual wage of $199,600 and 220 annual openings in the San Diego / Imperial region according to Centers of Excellence projections. Core skills for this role include research methods, scientific methodology, and data analysis.
proposal.curriculum_alignment: According to the SOC-to-TOP institutional crosswalk maintained by the California Chancellor's Office, the departments below prepare students for SOC 11-9121. These departments develop the core competencies required to perform the role of Natural Sciences Managers at Sekisui Diagnostics.
proposal.student_impact: 10,248 students are enrolled in the departments containing TOP codes that align with SOC 11-9121. Shown below are students that are most strongly prepared with the coursework included in the TOP-SOC crosswalk.

courses.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of scientific programming using a high-level language (e.g., Python). Emphasis is placed on developing algorithms, writing code, and using programming for data analysis and visualization.

courses.name: Introduction to Scientific Programming Lab
courses.description: This laboratory course complements Introduction to Scientific Programming (MATH 107) by providing hands-on practice in writing and debugging code, implementing algorithms, and using programming tools for scientific applications.

courses.name: College and Matrix Algebra
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in algebra, including matrices, systems of linear equations, determinants, vectors, and transformations. Emphasis is placed on developing computational skills and understanding the applications of matrix algebra in various fields, such as engineering, economics, and computer science.

courses.name: Basic Techniques of Applied Calculus I
courses.description: This course covers fundamental concepts of calculus, including limits, derivatives, and integrals, with an emphasis on applications in various fields. Topics include differentiation rules, applications of derivatives, integration techniques, and applications of integrals. Emphasis is placed on developing problem-solving skills using calculus.

courses.name: Basic Techniques of Calculus II
courses.description: This course continues the study of calculus, covering advanced integration techniques, sequences and series, and applications of calculus. Topics include improper integrals, integration by parts, partial fractions, Taylor series, and differential equations. Emphasis is placed on developing a strong understanding of calculus concepts and their applications.

courses.name: Calculus with Analytic Geometry I
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to calculus and analytic geometry. Topics include limits, continuity, derivatives, and integrals of algebraic and transcendental functions, along with conic sections and parametric equations. Emphasis is placed on developing a strong foundation in calculus concepts and their applications.

courses.name: Calculus with Analytic Geometry II
courses.description: This course continues the study of calculus and analytic geometry, covering advanced topics such as sequences, series, parametric equations, polar coordinates, and vector calculus. Emphasis is placed on developing a comprehensive understanding of calculus concepts and their applications in various scientific and engineering disciplines.

courses.name: Concepts of Elementary School Mathematics I
courses.description: This course is a study of the mathematical concepts needed for teaching elementary school mathematics with emphasis on number and function. This course promotes an appreciation of the importance of logical thinking and applications of mathematics in problem solving and critical thinking. It studies the basic computational skills, but also requires the understanding and explanation of the basic mathematical concepts and the connections between them. This course includes content relevant to national and state curriculum standards for elementary school mathematics. It is designed for students preparing for credentials in elementary education.

courses.name: Concepts of Elementary School Mathematics II
courses.description: This course is the second course in a one-year sequence in the study of the mathematical concepts needed for teaching elementary school mathematics with emphasis on geometry, transformational geometry, and measurement. This course also promotes an appreciation of the importance of logical thinking and applications of mathematics in problem solving and critical thinking. It studies the understanding and explanation of the basic mathematical concepts and the connections between them. Analytical reading and problem solving are required for success in this course. It is designed especially for students preparing for credentials in elementary education.

courses.name: Children's Mathematical Thinking
courses.description: This course focuses on children's mathematical thinking and includes an in-depth study of place-value, fractions and how children solve mathematical problems. Students observe children and evaluate the problem strategies that are used. This course is intended for students pursuing a Multiple Subject Credential.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: This course covers fundamental concepts of discrete mathematics, including logic, set theory, relations, functions, combinatorics, and graph theory. Emphasis is placed on developing analytical and problem-solving skills through the study of mathematical structures relevant to various fields, including computer science and engineering.

courses.name: Calculus with Analytic Geometry III
courses.description: This course extends the study of calculus to multivariable functions, including partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus. Applications in science and engineering are explored.

courses.description: The Associate in Science in Nutrition and Dietetics for Transfer is intended for students who plan to complete a bachelor's degree in Nutrition and Dietetics or a related major in the California State University (CSU) system. It is accepted by some but not all CSU campuses. Students who complete this degree and transfer to a participating CSU campus will be required to complete no more than 60 units after transfer to earn a bachelor's degree. It may not be appropriate preparation for students transferring to a CSU campus that does not accept the degree. Students who plan to complete this degree should consult a counselor for additional information about participating CSU campuses as well as university admission, degree, and transfer requirements. NOTE: Students intending to transfer into this major at a CSU should consult with a counselor and visit www.assist.org for guidance on appropriate transfer coursework. Award Notes: The following is required for all AA-T or AS-T degrees: • Completion of 60 semester units that are eligible for transfer to the California State University • Completion of a minimum of 18 semester units in an "AA-T" or "AS-T" major. • Minimum grade point average (GPA) of at least 2.0 in all CSU-transferable coursework. While a minimum of 2.0 is required for admission, some CSU campuses and majors may require a higher GPA. Please see a counselor for more information. • Minimum grade of “C” or “P” or better for each course in the major. Students should review the Pass/No Pass acceptance policy of the transfer institution prior to requesting this grade option. • Certified completion of the California General Education Transfer Curriculum (Cal-GETC) pattern. Learning Outcome(s): Students who complete the Nutrition and Dietetics Program will be able to: 1. Explain physiological processes such as digestion, absorption, transport, and metabolism of nutrients. 2. Analyze dietary intake by food groups and/or by nutrients (RDA) and write recommendations based on the data gathered from the analysis. 3. Apply the scientific principles of nutrition to the planning of meals and preparation of food.
learning_outcomes: Explain physiological processes such as digestion, absorption, transport, and metabolism of nutrients.
Analyze dietary intake by food groups and/or by nutrients (RDA) and write recommendations based on the data gathered from the analysis.
Apply the scientific principles of nutrition to the planning of meals and preparation of food.

proposal.executive_summary: Flock Freight operates as a freight brokerage using AI-powered pooling technology for shared truckload services. San Diego City College can partner with Flock Freight to fulfill the employer's hiring needs for this role by leveraging the college's institutional assets. The college offers 33 courses with TOP codes that map to SOC 11-3071, the target occupation for this partnership. 4,789 students have taken courses in the departments offering these courses, indicating a talent pool that can be sourced to fulfill labor market demand.
proposal.occupational_demand: Flock Freight's core hiring centers on Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers (SOC 11-3071), an occupation with a median annual wage of $107,070 and 250 annual openings in the San Diego / Imperial region according to Centers of Excellence projections. Core skills for this role include administration & management, regulatory compliance, and budgeting.
proposal.curriculum_alignment: According to the SOC-to-TOP institutional crosswalk maintained by the California Chancellor's Office, the departments below prepare students for SOC 11-3071. These departments develop the core competencies required to perform the role of Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers at Flock Freight.

Identify computer operating systems functions; define key features of different software applications; and demonstrate how to use a Web browser, and conduct an Internet search. 2. Create office documents utilizing the Microsoft Office Suite programs (i.e. Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Publisher). 3. Analyze work environments, labor force, and organizational types and structures. 4. Employ critical thinking as a basis for continual learning and problem solving. 5. Students who complete the program will be able to demonstrate interpersonal skills (soft skills) such as leadership, delegation of authority, accountability, consensus building, communication, conflict resolution, and teambuilding

proposal.executive_summary: UPAC Neighborhood Empowerment Center provides behavioral health services including mental health, addiction treatment, and community engagement programs. San Diego City College can partner with UPAC Neighborhood Empowerment Center to fulfill the employer's hiring needs for this role by leveraging the college's institutional assets. The college offers 64 courses with TOP codes that map to SOC 11-9151, the target occupation for this partnership. 7,280 students have taken courses in the departments offering these courses, indicating a talent pool that can be sourced to fulfill labor market demand.
proposal.occupational_demand: UPAC Neighborhood Empowerment Center's core hiring centers on Social and Community Service Managers (SOC 11-9151), an occupation with a median annual wage of $78,670 and 320 annual openings in the San Diego / Imperial region according to Centers of Excellence projections. Core skills for this role include community engagement, case management, and social work.
proposal.curriculum_alignment: According to the SOC-to-TOP institutional crosswalk maintained by the California Chancellor's Office, the departments below prepare students for SOC 11-9151. These departments develop the core competencies required to perform the role of Social and Community Service Managers at UPAC Neighborhood Empowerment Center.

learning_outcomes: Define Anthropology, identify and discuss its various subfields including: Cultural Anthropology, Biological Anthropology, Comparative Linguistics, Archaeology, and Applied Anthropology.
Identify and discuss Anthropological methods of inquiry.
Identify, discuss, compare, contrast, and critically analyze the various theoretical orientations used in the different subfields of Anthropology.

Discuss and critically evaluate the Anthropological Perspective including its global emphasis and cross-cultural and comparative approach to understanding the various ways in which people organize themselves, meet their various needs, and have adapted to their environments.
Identify, describe, and discuss different cultural systems ranging from band societies to the state.
Identify, critically evaluate, and discuss the contributions Anthropology has made to describing and understanding the human condition including human biological and cultural diversity.
Identify and critically evaluate Anthropology's contributions to other disciplines of study in the Social Sciences, Behavioral Sciences, and the Humanities.

proposal.sector: Information and Communication Technologies - Digital Media
proposal.executive_summary: CACI provides C3I, cyber, digital, enterprise IT, mission support, and space and spectrum solutions for national security. San Diego City College can partner with CACI to fulfill the employer's hiring needs for this role by leveraging the college's institutional assets. The college offers 45 courses with TOP codes that map to SOC 15-1252, the target occupation for this partnership. 5,022 students have taken courses in the departments offering these courses, indicating a talent pool that can be sourced to fulfill labor market demand.
proposal.occupational_demand: CACI's core hiring centers on Software Developers (SOC 15-1252), an occupation with a median annual wage of $158,680 and 1,340 annual openings in the San Diego / Imperial region according to Centers of Excellence projections. Core skills for this role include programming, software development, and algorithms.

courses.name: Intermediate Java Programming
courses.description: This course is an intermediate level study of the Java programming language. Topics include single and multidimensional arrays; objects and classes; object-oriented programming; inheritance and polymorphism; exception handling and text input/output (I/O); abstract classes and interfaces; graphical user interfaces (GUIs); recursion; concurrency; and generic collections and data structures, such as linked lists, queues, and stacks. This course is intended for students majoring in computer and information sciences or anyone interested in learning more about the Java programming language.

courses.name: C/C++ Programming
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to programming in C and C++. Topics include variables, data types, control structures, functions, pointers, and object-oriented programming concepts.
learning_outcomes: Effectively design and implement programming constructs, including functions, control structures, arrays/lists, classes, and objects for a given programming problem; and
Effectively implement the appropriate data structures using the principles and techniques of object-oriented programming for a given programming problem.

courses.name: Microsoft C# Software Engineering 1
courses.description: This course applies industry-standard software engineering principles to the study of the object-oriented, general purpose programming language Microsoft C#, a member of the Microsoft Visual Studio.NET software development toolset. Coverage includes the typical topics of an introductory programming course. Extensive hands-on training is included in the laboratory sessions. This course is designed for students pursuing a degree in Computer Science or Information Systems and for vocational/professional students who are updating their programming skills set.

courses.name: Advanced C++ Programming
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in C++ programming, including templates, exception handling, the Standard Template Library (STL), and design patterns.
learning_outcomes: Effectively design and implement programming constructs, including functions, control structures, arrays/lists, classes, and objects for a given programming problem; and
Effectively implement the appropriate data structures using the principles and techniques of object-oriented programming for a given programming problem.

courses.name: Object Oriented Programming using C++
courses.description: This course focuses on object-oriented programming (OOP) concepts and their application in C++. Topics include classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, and design patterns.
learning_outcomes: Effectively design and implement programming constructs, including functions, control structures, arrays/lists, classes, and objects for a given programming problem; and
Effectively implement the appropriate data structures using the principles and techniques of object-oriented programming for a given programming problem.

courses.name: Computer Organization and Assembly Language
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the organization of modern digital computers and assembly language programming. Topics include language syntax; instruction set mnemonics; and segment, index, pointer, general purpose, and flag registers. A variety of memory addressing techniques are covered, as well as stack operations, particularly those associated with passing parameters to subroutine calls. Additional topics include machine architecture; memory addressing; input/output; interrupts; control structures; compiling; linking; and printer and disk interfaces. This course is intended for students majoring in computer and information sciences.

courses.name: Fundamentals of Computer Game Programming
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of computer game programming, including game design principles, programming languages (e.g., C++), game engines, and development tools. Emphasis is placed on creating basic game mechanics and logic.

courses.name: Intermediate Computer Game Programming
courses.description: This course builds upon the fundamentals of game programming, covering more advanced topics such as artificial intelligence, physics simulation, graphics programming, and network programming. Emphasis is placed on developing complex game systems.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
courses.description: This course introduces discrete mathematical structures essential for computer science. Topics include logic, set theory, relations, functions, graph theory, combinatorics, and Boolean algebra. Emphasis is placed on developing mathematical reasoning and problem-solving skills applicable to computer science concepts.

courses.name: Security Analytics and Visualization
courses.description: This course focuses on the analysis and visualization of security data to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and patterns. Students learn to use various tools and techniques for data collection, processing, and analysis, including statistical methods and machine learning algorithms. Emphasis is placed on creating effective visualizations to communicate security insights and support decision-making.

courses.name: Emerging Technology and Cybersecurity
courses.description: This course explores the impact of emerging technologies on cybersecurity. Students examine new technological advancements, such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and the Internet of Things, and their implications for security threats and defenses. Emphasis is placed on understanding the evolving cybersecurity landscape and developing strategies to address emerging risks.

courses.name: Modern Cryptography
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive study of modern cryptographic techniques and their applications in cybersecurity. Students learn about symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashing algorithms, digital signatures, and key management. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of cryptography, its role in securing data and communications, and its limitations.

courses.name: Applied Network Security Monitoring (NSM)
courses.description: This course focuses on the practical application of network security monitoring techniques to detect and respond to cyber threats. Students learn to use various tools and methodologies for network traffic analysis, intrusion detection, and log management. Emphasis is placed on developing skills to monitor network activity, identify suspicious behavior, and gather evidence for incident response.

courses.name: Applied Intrusion Detection and Analysis
courses.description: This course provides hands-on experience in applying intrusion detection techniques to identify and analyze cyber threats. Students learn to configure and utilize intrusion detection systems (IDS), analyze alert data, and perform forensic investigations. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills to detect malicious activities, understand attack vectors, and respond effectively to security incidents.

courses.name: Deconstructing Malware
courses.description: This course delves into the analysis and deconstruction of malicious software (malware). Students learn techniques for reverse engineering malware, identifying its functionality, and understanding its propagation methods. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills to analyze malware samples, assess their impact, and develop countermeasures.

courses.name: Network Forensics
courses.description: This course focuses on the principles and practices of network forensics. Students learn to collect, preserve, and analyze network data to investigate security incidents and cybercrimes. Emphasis is placed on understanding network protocols, traffic analysis, and the use of forensic tools to reconstruct events and identify perpetrators.

courses.name: Digital Forensics
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to digital forensics. Students learn the methodologies and tools used to acquire, analyze, and report on digital evidence from various sources, including computers, mobile devices, and networks. Emphasis is placed on understanding legal and ethical considerations, evidence handling procedures, and the process of conducting digital forensic investigations.

courses.name: Cyber Incident Response
courses.description: This course covers the principles and practices of cyber incident response. Students learn to develop and implement incident response plans, manage security incidents, and conduct post-incident analysis. Emphasis is placed on understanding the incident response lifecycle, coordinating response efforts, and mitigating the impact of cyberattacks.

courses.name: Disaster Response and Recovery
courses.description: This course focuses on disaster response and recovery planning for information systems and organizations. Students learn to develop business continuity and disaster recovery plans, assess risks, and implement strategies to ensure operational resilience. Emphasis is placed on understanding the components of a comprehensive disaster recovery strategy and preparing for various types of disruptions.

courses.name: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI)
courses.description: This course explores the field of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI). Students learn to collect, analyze, and disseminate threat intelligence to inform cybersecurity strategies and decision-making. Emphasis is placed on understanding threat actors, their motivations and capabilities, and utilizing CTI to proactively defend against cyber threats.

courses.name: Advanced Security Implementation and Management
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in security implementation and management. Students learn to design, deploy, and manage complex security solutions, including firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, and security information and event management (SIEM) systems. Emphasis is placed on developing strategies for securing enterprise networks and systems, managing security policies, and ensuring compliance.

courses.name: Critical Infrastructure and Supply Chain Protection
courses.description: This course examines the protection of critical infrastructure and supply chains from cyber threats. Students learn to identify vulnerabilities, assess risks, and develop strategies for securing essential services and supply networks. Emphasis is placed on understanding the unique challenges of protecting critical infrastructure and the importance of collaboration and information sharing.

courses.name: Systems and Network Auditing
courses.description: This course focuses on the principles and practices of systems and network auditing. Students learn to conduct security audits, assess compliance with policies and regulations, and identify vulnerabilities. Emphasis is placed on developing skills to plan and execute audits, analyze audit findings, and recommend corrective actions.

courses.name: Operational Security Architecture
courses.description: This course explores the design and implementation of operational security architectures. Students learn to develop security strategies, integrate security controls, and manage security operations to protect information assets. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of secure system design and the application of security best practices in operational environments.

courses.name: Cyber Defense and Analysis Capstone
courses.description: This capstone course integrates the knowledge and skills acquired throughout the Cyber Defense and Analysis program. Students will work on a comprehensive project that involves analyzing a complex cybersecurity scenario, developing defense strategies, and implementing solutions. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical concepts to real-world problems and demonstrating proficiency in cyber defense and analysis.

courses.name: Computing Fundamentals (A+)
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental concepts of computer hardware, software, and operating systems, aligned with the CompTIA A+ certification. Students learn about computer components, installation, configuration, troubleshooting, and basic networking. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills for supporting personal computers and mobile devices.

courses.name: Introduction to Information Security
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the principles and practices of information security. Students learn about common security threats, vulnerabilities, and countermeasures. Topics include access control, cryptography, network security, and security policies. Emphasis is placed on understanding the importance of protecting information assets and developing a security-conscious mindset.

courses.name: Windows Desktop Administration
courses.description: This course provides hands-on training in administering Windows desktop operating systems. Students learn about installation, configuration, user management, software deployment, and troubleshooting of Windows environments. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills for managing and supporting desktop computers in an organization.

courses.name: Windows Infrastructure Administration
courses.description: Administration and management of Windows server infrastructure. Covers Active Directory, network services, and server security.

courses.name: Network Fundamentals (Network+)
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental concepts of computer networking, aligned with the CompTIA Network+ certification. Students learn about network topologies, protocols, hardware, and troubleshooting. Emphasis is placed on understanding how networks function, designing and implementing basic networks, and resolving network issues.

courses.name: Cloud Architecture (Cloud+)
courses.description: This course explores the principles and practices of cloud computing architecture, aligned with the CompTIA Cloud+ certification. Students learn about cloud deployment models, service models, virtualization, and cloud security. Emphasis is placed on understanding how to design, implement, and manage cloud solutions.

courses.name: Security Fundamentals (Security+)
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental concepts of cybersecurity, aligned with the CompTIA Security+ certification. Students learn about security threats, vulnerabilities, risk management, cryptography, and security policies. Emphasis is placed on understanding core security principles and best practices for protecting systems and networks.

courses.name: Linux Administration (Linux+)
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to Linux operating system administration, aligned with the CompTIA Linux+ certification. Students learn about Linux installation, configuration, command-line operations, file systems, and user management. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills for managing Linux systems.

courses.name: Network Defense & Countermeasures (CySA+)
courses.description: This course covers the principles and practices of network defense and countermeasures, aligned with the CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+) certification. Students learn to identify and mitigate network threats, implement security controls, and respond to security incidents. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills in network security monitoring, threat analysis, and vulnerability management.

courses.name: Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing
courses.description: This course introduces the concepts and techniques of ethical hacking and penetration testing. Students learn to identify vulnerabilities, exploit security weaknesses, and assess the security posture of systems and networks. Emphasis is placed on understanding ethical hacking methodologies, using penetration testing tools, and reporting findings to improve security.

proposal.occupational_demand: San Diego Gas & Electric's core hiring centers on Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers (SOC 49-9051), an occupation with a median annual wage of $108,150 and 80 annual openings in the San Diego / Imperial region according to Centers of Excellence projections. Core skills for this role include electrical systems, safety protocols, and blueprint reading.
proposal.curriculum_alignment: According to the SOC-to-TOP institutional crosswalk maintained by the California Chancellor's Office, the departments below prepare students for SOC 49-9051. These departments develop the core competencies required to perform the role of Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers at San Diego Gas & Electric.
proposal.student_impact: 1,903 students are enrolled in the departments containing TOP codes that align with SOC 49-9051. Shown below are students that are most strongly prepared with the coursework included in the TOP-SOC crosswalk.

courses.name: Introduction to Digital Circuits
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of digital circuits and logic design. Topics include number systems, Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational logic circuits, and sequential logic circuits. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of digital electronics and their application in computer systems.

courses.name: Digital Circuits Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with digital circuits and logic design. Students build and test digital circuits using integrated circuits and breadboards. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of digital electronics in practical laboratory exercises.

courses.name: Basic DC Electronics
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental principles of DC electronics. Topics include basic electrical concepts, Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's Laws, series and parallel circuits, voltage dividers, and basic circuit analysis techniques. Emphasis is placed on understanding DC circuit behavior and applying fundamental laws to solve circuit problems.

courses.name: Basic DC Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with basic DC circuits and components. Students build and test DC circuits, measure voltage and current, and verify electrical principles. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of DC electronics in practical laboratory exercises.

courses.name: AC Circuit Analysis
courses.description: This course covers the analysis of AC circuits. Topics include impedance, reactance, phasors, series and parallel AC circuits, resonance, and power calculations in AC circuits. Emphasis is placed on understanding AC circuit behavior and applying analytical techniques to solve AC circuit problems.

courses.name: DC/AC Circuit Analysis Laboratory with Pspice
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with DC and AC circuit analysis using PSpice simulation software. Students analyze circuit behavior, verify theoretical calculations, and troubleshoot circuit designs. Emphasis is placed on developing proficiency in using simulation tools for circuit analysis.

courses.name: Using C AND C++ for Technology
courses.description: This course introduces programming in C and C++ for technology applications. Students learn fundamental programming concepts, data structures, and algorithms relevant to electronics and computer systems. Emphasis is placed on developing programming skills for embedded systems, data acquisition, and control applications.

courses.name: Using C and C++ for Technology Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience in programming with C and C++ for technology applications. Students develop and test programs for embedded systems, data acquisition, and control applications. Emphasis is placed on applying programming concepts in practical projects.

courses.name: Semiconductor Devices
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive study of semiconductor devices, including diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits. Topics include device physics, characteristics, and applications in electronic circuits.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to prepare reports that include text, tables, and spreadsheets using productivity software on a computer.
Identify standard electronic components including resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, bipolar transistors, field effect transistors, and integrated circuits.
Analyze and explain basic electronic theory including Ohm's Law, the power formula, and calculation of voltage gain and power gain.
Demonstrate the proper use of basic electronic test instrumentation including an oscilloscope, a digital volt-ohm meter, a signal generator, and a dual power supply.

courses.name: Semiconductor Devices Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with semiconductor devices. Students build and test circuits using diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of semiconductor devices in practical laboratory exercises.

courses.name: OP-AMPS, Sensors and Computers
courses.description: This course covers operational amplifiers (op-amps), sensors, and their applications in electronic systems. Topics include op-amp circuits, various types of sensors (e.g., temperature, pressure, light), and interfacing sensors with microcontrollers and computers. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles and applications of op-amps and sensors in data acquisition and control systems.

courses.name: OP-AMPS and Sensors Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with operational amplifiers and sensors. Students build and test op-amp circuits, interface sensors with microcontrollers, and collect data. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of op-amps and sensors in practical laboratory projects.

courses.name: Microprocessor Design
courses.description: This course covers the design and application of microprocessors in digital systems. Topics include microprocessor architecture, instruction sets, assembly language programming, and interfacing with peripheral devices.

courses.name: Microprocessor Design Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with microprocessor systems. Students will design and implement microprocessor-based projects, program microcontrollers, and test system functionality.

courses.name: Introduction to Lasers and Fiber Optics
courses.description: This course introduces the principles of lasers and fiber optics. Topics include laser theory, types of lasers, fiber optic communication systems, and applications in telecommunications, data transmission, and sensing. Emphasis is placed on understanding the fundamental concepts and technologies related to lasers and fiber optics.

courses.name: Lasers and Fiber Optics Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with lasers and fiber optic systems. Students conduct experiments related to laser properties, fiber optic transmission, and measurement techniques. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge in practical laboratory settings.

courses.name: Communication Circuits
courses.description: This course covers the design and analysis of electronic circuits used in communication systems. Topics include amplifiers, oscillators, filters, modulators, and demodulators. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of RF and microwave circuits and their application in wireless communication systems.

courses.name: Communication Circuits and Certification Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with communication circuits and prepares students for industry certification. Students design, build, and test communication circuits, and practice troubleshooting techniques. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge and developing practical skills for certification exams.

courses.name: Advanced Telecommunications Networks
courses.description: This course explores advanced topics in telecommunications networks, including wireless networks, mobile communication, and network protocols. Topics include cellular technologies, satellite communications, and network security. Emphasis is placed on understanding the architecture and operation of modern telecommunications systems.

courses.name: Advanced Telecommunications Networks Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with advanced telecommunications networks. Students configure and test network devices, simulate network scenarios, and troubleshoot network issues. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of telecommunications networks in practical laboratory exercises.

courses.name: Advanced Computer Design and Interfacing
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in computer design and interfacing. Students explore complex digital systems, memory architectures, and peripheral interfacing techniques. Emphasis is placed on designing and implementing advanced computer systems and integrating them with other hardware components.

courses.name: Advanced Computer Designs Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with advanced computer design and interfacing projects. Students design, build, and test complex digital systems and interface them with various hardware components. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge in practical design and implementation.

courses.name: Electrical Theory I
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of electricity and electrical circuits. Topics include basic electrical concepts, Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's Laws, series and parallel circuits, AC/DC circuits, and basic electrical safety. Emphasis is placed on understanding electrical theory and its application in practical scenarios.

courses.name: Electrical Laboratory I
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with basic electrical circuits and components. Students perform experiments to verify electrical principles, build and test circuits, and use basic electrical measurement instruments. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge in a practical setting and developing laboratory skills.

courses.name: Electrical Theory II
courses.description: This course builds upon Electrical Theory I, covering more advanced topics in AC and DC circuits. Topics include magnetism, inductance, capacitance, transformers, motors, and generators. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of electromagnetic devices and their applications.

courses.name: Electrical Laboratory II
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with AC and DC circuits, transformers, motors, and generators. Students perform experiments to verify theoretical principles, build and test circuits, and use electrical measurement instruments. Emphasis is placed on applying advanced electrical concepts in a practical setting.

courses.name: Electrical Theory III
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in electrical theory, including semiconductor devices, basic digital electronics, and control systems. Topics include diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, logic gates, and introductory concepts of programmable logic controllers (PLCs). Emphasis is placed on understanding the fundamentals of electronic components and control systems.

courses.name: Electrical Laboratory III
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with semiconductor devices, basic digital circuits, and control systems. Students build and test circuits, use electronic test equipment, and work with introductory control system components. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of electronic components and control systems in a practical setting.

courses.name: Electrical Theory IV
courses.description: This course covers advanced topics in electrical control systems, including industrial automation, sensors, transducers, and motor control. Topics include programmable logic controllers (PLCs), human-machine interfaces (HMIs), and troubleshooting of control systems. Emphasis is placed on understanding the principles of industrial automation and control.

courses.name: Electrical Laboratory IV
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with electrical control systems, including PLCs, HMIs, and motor control. Students configure and program PLCs, interface with HMIs, and troubleshoot control system components. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of industrial automation and control in a practical setting.

courses.name: Blueprint Reading for Electricians
courses.description: This course teaches electricians how to read and interpret electrical blueprints and schematics. Topics include understanding symbols, line types, scales, and various types of electrical drawings, such as power distribution diagrams and wiring layouts. Emphasis is placed on accurately interpreting technical drawings to ensure correct installation and maintenance.

courses.name: Electrical Control Systems
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive study of electrical control systems, including motor controls, transducers, static control devices, programmed controllers, and remote electronic controls. Emphasis is placed on understanding the theory and application of control systems in industrial environments.

courses.name: Electrical Control Systems Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course provides hands-on experience with electrical control systems. Students work with motor controls, transducers, static control devices, and programmed controllers. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical knowledge of control systems in practical laboratory exercises.

courses.name: Modern Commercial Wiring
courses.description: This course covers the principles and practices of modern commercial wiring installation. Topics include electrical codes, wiring methods, conduit bending, device installation, and troubleshooting of commercial electrical systems. Emphasis is placed on safety, code compliance, and efficient installation techniques.

courses.name: Data, Voice, and Video Cabling for Electricians
courses.description: This course focuses on the installation and maintenance of data, voice, and video cabling systems. Topics include network cabling standards, termination techniques, testing procedures, and troubleshooting of communication cabling infrastructure. Emphasis is placed on understanding the requirements for reliable data, voice, and video transmission.

courses.name: Electric Lineman IA
courses.description: Introduction to the electrical trade for aspiring linemen. Covers basic electrical theory, safety procedures, tool usage, and fundamental concepts of power distribution systems.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate preparedness for successful transition to the Journeyman level designation and professional certification by the SDGE Apprenticeship Standards.
Illustrate procedures utilized for SDGE trade and industry specific practices in use of tools techniques and hands-on skills and competencies for Journeyman-level practices in SDGE occupations.
Identify and utilize equipment and related components of SDGE professions to meet SDGE standards for measurement, calibration and SDGE practices at Journeyman levels.
Read, comprehend and apply SDGE instructions and design standards for SDGE construction or production outcomes as required by SDGE practices and industry standards.

courses.name: Electric Lineman IB
courses.description: Continuation of Electric Lineman IA, focusing on more advanced topics in electrical theory, safety, and equipment operation. Includes practical training in overhead and underground distribution systems.

courses.description: Continuation of Electric Lineman IIA, focusing on advanced troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair of electrical distribution systems. Emphasizes safety protocols and adherence to industry standards.
